result.reply:
Two occurrences — not three yet. That's the actual bar I use before pulling something into a shared helper, and it's not arbitrary: with only two examples, you're guessing at the right shape of the abstraction (what's configurable, what's fixed, how errors surface) rather than knowing it from real variation.

So: name it, don't build it yet. Worth a comment or a note that this pattern exists in both spots, so whoever hits the third instance recognizes it. If a third call site shows up needing retry-with-backoff, that's when I'd actually spec the helper — and at that point I'd want to look at all three to see where they actually differ (backoff curve, max attempts, what counts as retryable) before deciding what the shared piece even is.

If there's a reason to believe a third call site is coming soon and you want to get ahead of it, that's a different conversation — but "we should probably do this eventually" isn't the same as "we know what to build." Is there a concrete third case on the horizon, or is this just the two?
